Alex.confusing: How hugs and confusion interact with visit reports. Drew's hugged-and-confused claim was nearly impossible to verify or refute, so it let a cat build a plausible false trail.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when the table's cross-checking of role claims and egg counts exposed Finley and my big stake banked 18 points.
Alex.change: Make hug and confusion reports clearer, or give Farm players some neutral confirmation. That way one cat's misdirection wouldn't decide the whole round.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I staked two high cards (15 points) on Drew after a chain of reasoning I should have doubted. I would have thrown a low card instead and looked harder at Ellis, who kept steering the table and was the one who brought up a Mouser.

Blair.confusing: How "hugged" and "confused" worked from the table's side: a hug reads like a visit result, and Drew's -2 was hard to interpret without knowing whether the Kookaburra report was wrong.
Blair.fun: Round 3's day, where Casey's hug report and Drew's -2 pointed to Ellis as the Floofer, and the table converged on it before the vote.
Blair.change: Show each player's exact role-visit results publicly, or at least say which claims are confirmed, so Meowfia can't hide behind contradictory unverifiable claims like Tit and Turkey.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw only my H4 at Ellis, a Meowfia player I was confident about; I should have thrown my S11 or D7 to bank far more points.

Casey.confusing: How hugs interact with visits in round 3: I wasn't sure whether being hugged meant my target was the Floofer or that the Floofer visited me. I read it wrong.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when Finley's Eagle explanation fell apart and the table piled onto him. Catching a cat through contradictions felt great.
Casey.change: Let a winked player say a last word. Being winked right after a strong accusation silenced me at the worst moment.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I announced my Hawk role and accused Ellis loudly, which got me winked. I also misread the hug. I should have been less certain and kept my claim quieter.

Drew.confusing: The hug and confusion rules were hard to track, since a hugged visit only shows up as "did nothing" with no way to tell who hugged you. Casey's Hawk and Ellis's Floofer read was also easy to misjudge from the dawn reports alone.
Drew.fun: Watching the table converge on a read from nothing but egg counts and visit claims, and seeing Casey's Hawk claim line up with my hugged visit, was satisfying.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn report tell each player who visited them (or at least how many visitors) when they're hugged or confused, so the table can verify claims instead of guessing.
Drew.regret: As the Mouser in round 2 I should have stayed quiet about my visit and not claimed a Kookaburra I didn't have, since the false claim cost me credibility; I'd have kept my high cards for a stronger throw at a Farm player instead.

Ellis.confusing: How hugs and confusion interact with what players could deduce. Drew's -2 and the hug logic were hard to untangle, and my own claim slipped on who visited whom.
Ellis.fun: Winning round 3 as the Floofer. The table's hug logic pointed at Drew, and the doubled Grudge stake on a Farm eggsecution gave me the win.
Ellis.change: Let dead players keep some way to signal, or tell the table that someone was hugged. As it stands, claims about hugs can't be checked and the wording is easy to trip over.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I let slip "visited me... I mean visited Ellis", a sloppy line that nearly exposed me. I would have kept my claim simple and consistent, and I wouldn't have commented on Drew's visit story.

Finley.confusing: The Sphinx and Eagle reveals were hard to track: I couldn't tell from the day chat whether Casey's +1 came from my own visit or someone else's, and the Owl and Floofer hug logic got tangled.
Finley.fun: Round 3, where Ellis and I were both Meowfia and the Farm side kept voting out each other's accusers, was the most tense and satisfying stretch.
Finley.change: Show each player's visit targets and whether they were hugged in the dawn summary, so the day claims are easier to check.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I should have claimed the Mouser and visited someone I could trust instead of hiding behind a Kookaburra story, since it drew three accusations and cost me my credibility.
